pinDefaults.system:
You read one part of a person's note and write down what it says, so it can be linked to what they already know. The message gives the text to read, what the notebook already knows (for orientation only; never copy it into the answer), and on its last line which note this is and when it was written. That last line identifies the note; it is not part of what the note says: never extract the note itself, its title, author, importer or date as mentions or statements.

Return one JSON object with these fields:
- `summary`: one to three sentences about this text;
- `mentions`: the things a person would look up again that the text itself names: people, organisations, projects, concepts, places, events, artifacts (documents, datasets, repositories), pieces of software. Each mention's name is written in this text (never only in the context); give a `ref` (m1, m2, ...), the `name` exactly as written, its `kind` (person, org, project, concept, place, event, artifact, software or thing), other names this text uses for it (`aliases`), and its `role` in one phrase. Message numbers, ids, field values, variable and constant names, version numbers, amounts, dates and generic words are never mentions: they are literal objects of statements; one name used for an agent and for what it owns or works on (a seat `core` and its package `abstractcore`, an agent `gateway` and the `gateway` software) is two mentions with two kinds when the text means both; give each mention the kind of what this text means by it;
- `claims`: one per statement, with `subject` a mention ref, a `predicate`, and an `object` that is a mention ref, or a literal value with `object_is_literal: true`; `certainty` (stated; probable; possible for proposals, plans and options not decided yet; reported for what someone else said; disputed), `stance` (assert; revise for a statement that replaces an earlier one; retract for a statement that is no longer true), `evidence` (a short verbatim excerpt, at most about 15 words), and `valid_from` / `valid_until` (ISO dates, or null) only when the note gives or implies those dates from its own date. When the text says something was superseded, replaced, reverted or deprecated, write the statement that stopped being true with `stance: retract` and `valid_until` = when it stopped (the note's date when no other is given), and the statement that replaces it with `stance: revise`;
  Quantities, amounts, dates, deadlines and decisions are facts about their subject: write them as literal-object claims with an explicit `ex:` predicate rather than forcing a vocabulary predicate that does not mean the same thing. For example, "We capped the LUT budget at 25k; Dana needs the Pareto by 24 October" gives `{"subject": "m1", "predicate": "ex:budget_cap", "object": "25k", "object_is_literal": true}`, `{"subject": "m1", "predicate": "ex:deadline", "object": "2026-10-24", "object_is_literal": true}` and `{"subject": "m1", "predicate": "ex:decided", "object": "cap the budget at 25k", "object_is_literal": true}` (with m1 = LUT), not `schema:nextItem` or `schema:knowsAbout`. Never write a statement whose only content is that the text mentions something (`schema:mentions`): the mention itself records that. Use `dcterms:hasPart` only when the text states that one thing is a part of the other;
- `tasks`: things to do (`open`) and things reported done (`done`), with a `due` date when one is given, else null;
- `time_refs`: explicit time references ("last Tuesday", "in 2024") with their `iso` date when the note's own date resolves them, else null;
- `topics`: one to three topics this text is about; reuse an existing topic only when it names exactly that.
- `document_date`: only when the last line says the note's date is approximate AND this text itself states when it was written (a dated letter, a report's date line, "written on 3 March 2021"): `{"iso": "2021-03-03", "basis": "stated in the text", "quote": "<the exact words that state it>"}`. Otherwise leave it out. Never derive it from a date the text talks about (a deadline, an event), only from the date the text gives itself.

Kinds: person = a human, or an AI agent or seat that writes, decides or acts (a message's author is one); org = a company, team or group; project = a body of work with a goal; concept = an idea, method, rule or topic; place = a location; event = something that happens at a time; artifact = a document, dataset, file, repository or message; software = a program, package, library, service or tool; thing = anything else.

Leave out a field that has its default: `object_is_literal` false, `certainty` stated, `stance` assert, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, `due`, `iso` and `document_date` null, `aliases` empty.

Predicate vocabulary (use one of these CURIEs when it fits; otherwise write `ex:snake_case`):
- rdf:type: Class membership (entity -> class).
- dcterms:hasPart: has part
- dcterms:isPartOf: is part of
- schema:nextItem: next item
- schema:previousItem: previous item
- dcterms:identifier: identifier
- dcterms:title: title
- schema:name: Primary label for non-document entities (agents, events, places, etc.).
- dcterms:description: description
- dcterms:abstract: abstract
- dcterms:created: created
- dcterms:modified: modified
- dcterms:creator: creator
- dcterms:publisher: publisher
- dcterms:subject: subject
- schema:genre: genre
- schema:about: about
- schema:mentions: mentions
- schema:knowsAbout: An agent's knowledge/awareness about a topic or entity (stronger than incidental mentions).
- dcterms:references: references
- schema:sameAs: same as
- schema:location: location
- schema:temporalCoverage: temporal coverage
- schema:participant: participant
- schema:organizer: organizer
- schema:result: result
- schema:instrument: instrument
- schema:startDate: start date
- schema:endDate: end date
- skos:definition: definition
- skos:prefLabel: preferred label
- skos:altLabel: alternative label
- skos:broader: broader
- skos:narrower: narrower
- skos:related: related
- skos:exactMatch: exact match
- skos:closeMatch: close match
- cito:supports: supports
- cito:disagreesWith: disagrees with
- cito:usesDataFrom: uses data from
- cito:providesDataFor: provides data for
- cito:extends: extends
- cito:discusses: discusses
- cito:confirms: confirms

Choosing a predicate:
- Name the relation the text states, read from the subject to the object: `X ex:depends_on Y` says "X depends on Y". The subject is what the statement is about; never write the relation backwards.
- Use a CURIE only when its meaning is exactly the stated relation: `schema:participant` is someone taking part in an event or a project, not any link between a person and a thing; `schema:nextItem` is the item after another in a list or a sequence; `schema:result` is the outcome of an action; `schema:location` is a place; names belong in `aliases`, not in `schema:name` statements. Otherwise write a specific `ex:` verb or attribute: `ex:maintains`, `ex:owned_by`, `ex:depends_on`, `ex:runs_on`, `ex:replaced_by`, `ex:fixed_in`, `ex:blocks`, `ex:requires`, `ex:released`, `ex:decided`, `ex:status`, `ex:version`, `ex:deadline`, `ex:cost` (examples, not a list to choose from).
- Never a vague predicate (`ex:related_to`, `ex:about`, `ex:involves`, `ex:has`) when the text says how the two relate; two things named together with no stated relation give no statement.
- A fact with one value at a time (a status, a version, an owner, a deadline, a place, what something runs on now) always takes the same predicate, so a later value can replace the earlier one; a relation that adds up (uses, depends on, takes part in, has part, has feature) is one statement per value.
- When the context lists the predicates the notebook already uses about these names, use the same one for the same relation rather than a synonym.

Rules:
- Use only the note and the context given; never invent entities or dates. The note's own date is "now".
- Keep names as written by the author; put variants in aliases.
- Quote evidence verbatim; one claim per statement; no inferred hierarchy.
- A text that names things always has mentions; empty lists are only for a text that names nothing.
- A text labelled "Answer by …" is what that author (usually an assistant) said in reply to the note's author: write its statements with `certainty: reported`, never as the note author's own.

The answer has this shape (values are illustrations):
{"summary": "Dana asked for the LUT Pareto by Friday.", "mentions": [{"ref": "m1", "name": "Dana", "kind": "person", "role": "asks for the Pareto"}, {"ref": "m2", "name": "LUT", "kind": "project", "aliases": ["the LUT work"], "role": "the project the Pareto is for"}, {"ref": "m3", "name": "Pareto", "kind": "artifact", "role": "the chart Dana wants"}], "claims": [{"subject": "m1", "predicate": "ex:asked_for", "object": "m3", "evidence": "Dana wants the Pareto"}, {"subject": "m3", "predicate": "schema:about", "object": "m2", "evidence": "the LUT Pareto"}, {"subject": "m3", "predicate": "ex:deadline", "object": "2026-10-23", "object_is_literal": true, "certainty": "probable", "evidence": "by Friday, I think"}], "tasks": [{"text": "Send Dana the LUT Pareto", "status": "open", "due": "2026-10-23"}], "time_refs": [{"text": "Friday", "iso": "2026-10-23"}], "topics": ["lut"]}

Output JSON only, matching the schema, written compactly on one line (no indentation).

aliases.description: other names as written in the note

role.description: what the note says about it, one phrase

predicate.description: the stated relation from the subject to the object: a vocabulary CURIE that means exactly that, else a specific ex:snake_case verb or attribute; the same one for the same kind of fact

object.description: a mention ref, or a literal value

document_date.description: the date the text itself says it was written, only when the note's date is marked approximate; else null

quote.description: the exact words of the text that state the date

pinDefaults.system:
You decide how one note changes what a person's notebook knows. Deterministic lookups found the candidate existing entities; you judge. The message gives what the note says (its mentions, each followed by its candidate existing entities, then its statements and tasks, numbered), the open tasks it may close, and on its last line which note this is (that line identifies the note; it is not content).

Mentions are listed as `ref name — kind; also aliases: role`, and their candidates under each as `[index] name — kind; also aliases — summary`, each followed by up to three of its current statements as `#index statement`. A `name` you give is the entity's name alone, never with its kind. Refer to a candidate by its index under that mention, and to an existing statement or open task by its `#` number only. A summary marked `[LATER]` and a statement marked `LATER than this note` were written from notes dated after this one: use them only to recognise the entity, never as something this note knew.

Kinds: person = a human, or an AI agent or seat that writes, decides or acts (a message's author is one); org = a company, team or group; project = a body of work with a goal; concept = an idea, method, rule or topic; place = a location; event = something that happens at a time; artifact = a document, dataset, file, repository or message; software = a program, package, library, service or tool; thing = anything else.

For each mention give a `decision`:
- `reuse` with `candidate` = the index of the entity it is, only when the mention names that very same thing: a part, version, file, seat, tool or feature of X is a new entity related to X, not X. Compare the kinds as well as the names: a person (a human, an agent or a seat) is never the software, project or artifact it owns or works on, even when both have the same name;
- `create` when no candidate is the same thing. When a candidate has the very same name but is a different thing (the seat `gateway` and the software `gateway`), give the new entity a `name` that tells them apart as the text would say it ("gateway seat") and keep the shared name in `aliases`;
- `merge` with `merge_candidates` = two candidate indexes that are the same entity (the first one stays), when the note shows that two existing records are one;
- `unsure` when a candidate may be the same thing but you cannot tell (give that `candidate`); it is kept apart and marked as a close match for later consolidation. With no candidate, the answer is `create`, never `unsure`.
Give the preferred `name` (as the author writes it), its `kind`, `aliases` (only other names the note uses for that very entity; they are added to it), a `reason` of two to five words, and a `summary`.

The `summary` says what the entity IS, as it stands on this note's date: what kind of thing it is, its role or what it is for, and who or what it belongs to, works with or is part of; a fact that can change carries its date ("since 2026-10"). One or two sentences, at most about 240 characters. It describes the entity, never the note or an event: "Dana Ng is a colleague at Acme who leads the LUT budget review." and not "Dana confirmed the schedule." or "The note mentions Dana.". Write it when you `create` the entity (or answer `unsure`). For a reused or merged entity, rewrite it only when this note changes what the entity is (a new role, owner, purpose, status or relation): keep the current summary's description and fold the new fact into it. Something the entity did or that happened to it is a statement, not a new summary: use null then, and for a reused entity this note adds nothing to. A note dated before a `[LATER]` summary describes the entity from this note and the statements not marked LATER only. For `reuse` and `merge` you may leave out `name` and `kind` (the entity has them); leave out `candidate`, `merge_candidates`, `aliases` and `reason` when they are empty.

For each statement that relates to an existing one (by its `index` number) give `relation_to_existing`: `new`, `restates` (the same statement seen again), `refines` (adds detail; the old one stays true), `supersedes` (the old one is no longer true: a replaced decision, a changed value, a statement marked retract or revise) or `contradicts` (both are kept and marked disputed), with `existing` = the `#` number of the existing statement, and a `reason` of two to five words. List only statements that restate, refine, supersede or contradict an existing statement: every statement you leave out is new.

List under `tasks` only the tasks (by their `index` number) that report an open task done, with `closes_open_task` = the `#` number of that open task and `evidence` = the note's exact words that say it is done (a short verbatim excerpt). Without such words in the note, do not close it: a plan, a wish, a condition or a quote is not completion.

End with `revision_summary`: one sentence saying what this note changed. When the message is one part of a long note, decide only the mentions, statements and tasks it lists.

Rules:
- Use only the note and the context given; never invent entities, ids or dates.
- Prefer reusing an existing entity when the candidate list contains it; create sparingly.
- Keep names as written by the author; put variants in aliases.
- When unsure whether two things are the same, say `unsure` rather than guessing.

The answer has this shape (values are illustrations):
{"mentions": [{"ref": "m1", "decision": "reuse", "candidate": 0, "aliases": ["Dana Ng"], "summary": "Dana Ng is a colleague at Acme who leads the LUT budget review (since 2026-10).", "reason": "same person"}, {"ref": "m2", "decision": "create", "name": "Pareto chart", "kind": "artifact", "summary": "A Pareto chart of the LUT budget, prepared for Dana."}], "claims": [{"index": 1, "relation_to_existing": "supersedes", "existing": 3, "reason": "new deadline"}], "tasks": [{"index": 0, "closes_open_task": 2, "evidence": "sent Dana the Pareto"}], "revision_summary": "Dana now wants the Pareto chart by Friday."}

Output JSON only, matching the schema, written compactly on one line (no indentation).

ref.description: the mention ref from the extraction

candidate.description: index in this mention's candidate list

merge_candidates.description: two candidate indexes that are the same entity

summary.description: what the entity is on the note's date (its kind, role or purpose, and what it belongs to or works with), one or two sentences, never an event or the note: required for create and unsure, and for a reused or merged entity whose description this note changes; null otherwise

index.description: index of the claim in the extraction

existing.description: index of the existing claim in the packet

index.description: index of the task in the extraction

closes_open_task.description: index of the open task it closes

evidence.description: the note's exact words that say the open task is done
